A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIM-CoT research, with matching core components and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original AIMCoT benchmark results, component ablations, attention analyses, sensitivity experiments and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds backbone evaluations, evidence-alignment measurements, robustness experiments and safeguard ablations.

M1.justification: The core CAG, entropy-based greedy AVP and attention-shift DAT procedures remain. v2 adds explicit negative constraints to the CAG prompt, safety instructions accompanying visual insertion, and an optional adaptive Z-score trigger (Sections 4.2–4.4; Appendix G.1). Fixed thresholds remain the main experimental configuration.

E1.justification: The three VQA benchmarks remain M3CoT, ScienceQA and LLaVA-W. v2 adds test scenarios with adversarially corrupted attention and irrelevant patches injected from other samples (Appendices I.3 and L.2). These extend input-condition coverage without introducing a new application domain.

E2.justification: The main comparator roster remains No-CoT, DDCoT, MMCoT, CCoT, SCAFFOLD and ICoT; candidate-construction alternatives also remain. v2 adds evaluated controls without CAG constraints and without insertion safety instructions in Tables 19–20, extending comparisons within the framework.

E3.justification: v2 adds Janus-Pro-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-32B configurations and introduces SAM-overlap evaluation, randomized blind GPT-4v comparisons, and noise-injection protocols. The masking study changes from Chameleon/LLaVA-W with Kmask up to 20 to four-backbone averages on M3CoT/ScienceQA with Kmask up to 50. Main accuracy/ROUGE-L metrics and 0-/1-shot settings remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds evidence-alignment analyses, CAG-description-length sensitivity, adaptive-trigger comparisons, adversarial attention tests, safeguard ablations and a ScienceQA reasoning case study (Figure 6). Component ablations and runtime sensitivity also extend to additional backbones. Earlier candidate-source and approximate-submodularity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports correlation, t-test and binomial-test results. v2 additionally reports paired McNemar and Wilcoxon significance tests for the main benchmark comparisons, with markers and detailed statistics (Tables 1 and 10), plus Wilcoxon tests for attention alignment. The three-repeat candidate-source analysis is retained; increased experimental run counts are not established.

E6.justification: The original two backbones' raw headline scores remain, while new backbone, alignment, robustness, adaptive-trigger and timing results substantially expand the findings. BM with CAG scores change from 30.3 to 30.1 on M3CoT and from 52.0 to 51.5 on ScienceQA (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 3). Masking results are replaced under different evaluation conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds the formal definition and decision rule for the adaptive Z-score trigger. The entropy definitions, diminishing-returns inequalities and complexity derivation are otherwise retained. Despite its expanded optimality framing, Appendix I.4 provides no new greedy-optimality theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains active information-driven selection combined with dynamic insertion timing. v2 explicitly adds resistance to noisy attention and descriptions to its introduction's contribution claims. The additional backbone results support the retained general superiority claim rather than redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations of architecture- and scale-dependent gains, semantic and human-intuition alignment, and resistance to error propagation (Sections 5.5–5.6; Appendices K–L). It strengthens the CAG–AVP interaction interpretation to explicit super-additivity using revised scores. v1's concluding caveat about further long-form reasoning evaluation disappears, although computational overhead remains discussed.

D1.justification: v2 documents the revised CAG prompt, GPT-4v judging prompt, additional patch/grid mapping details, and adaptive-trigger parameters W=5 and lambda=3. Core hyperparameters and the stated code link remain. v1's A6000 GPU disclosure is absent from v2.

R1.justification: v2 condenses related work around ICoT and explicitly acknowledges adopting its established interleaving paradigm. It adds citations on recent VLM reasoning, additional backbones, automated judges and perturbation attribution, while removing MRFD and several other cited works. The fundamental positioning around active selection and dynamic triggering remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation and method exposition are extensively rewritten around what to see and when to see it. Experimental setup is consolidated, the greedy algorithm moves into the main text, and retained appendices are reorganized by topic. The separate LLM-usage statement is removed.

P2.justification: v2 changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, replaces the AVP-only schematic with a full-framework overview, redraws the CAG illustration and adds the Figure 6 reasoning case. Restaurant illustrations are rearranged, runtime tables are merged and transposed, and the main results table becomes a four-backbone panel display.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central selection mechanism: v1's largely illustrative alignment argument gains SAM-overlap measurements, blind GPT-4v comparisons and controlled noise/safeguard experiments. Additional backbones, ablations and paired significance reporting also strengthen generalization and empirical support. These gains outweigh the lost hardware disclosure and remaining interpretive limitations: human alignment uses automated proxies, and architecture/scale explanations are not established by controlled causal comparisons.
